The blank in the sentence 'Helen________ with her son at 7 o’clock tonight.' requires a verb tense that expresses an action happening at a specific future time. The correct tense for an action that will be in progress at a particular moment in the future is the 'future continuous' tense: will be + V-ing.
  • was playing (verb (past continuous)): Past continuous tense, used for actions that were happening at a specific time in the past.
  • will play (verb (simple future)): Simple future tense, used for actions that will happen in the future but not necessarily in progress at a specific time.
  • will be playing (verb (future continuous)): Future continuous tense, used for actions that will be happening at a specific time in the future.
Related structure or vocabulary: Future continuous tense: will be + V-ing. Used to describe an action that will be in progress at a specific time in the future.
